system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: How much of the zero-shot localisation quality of MVFA (pixel AUROC and Dice on a held-out modality) is retained when its segmentation adapters are trained without pixel masks, using pseudo-masks drawn only from labelled abnormal source images (a patch is anomalous when its frozen CLIP level-4 feature is farther from every normal patch of the same dataset than the 99th percentile of normal-to-normal nearest-neighbour distances on source validation data), as masks are removed from zero, one, or all three masked source datasets?

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Cross-level persistence pseudo-masks: anomalies that persist across MVFA's four feature levels
SUMMARY: Mark a patch as anomalous only if its nearest-neighbour distance exceeds the normal threshold at three or more of the four CLIP levels that MVFA adapts, because lesions are anomalous at several levels of abstraction while normal-but-rare patterns usually stand out at one.
HYPOTHESIS: Cross-level persistence (at least 3 of 4 levels) raises pseudo-mask precision by at least 15 points over level-4-only pseudo-masks at a recall loss below 10 points, and MVFA trained on persistence masks recovers at least 90% of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC on held-out masked modalities.
RATIONALE: The occlusion parent asks which patches drive the detection decision. By analogy with persistence in topological data analysis and multi-scale feature detection, where real structures persist across scales and noise does not, a lesion should be anomalous in low-level texture features (layer 6), mid-level (12, 18) and semantic features (24), whereas a normal structure that is merely rare in the bank, or an imaging artefact, tends to be anomalous at only one level. MVFA already uses exactly these four levels, so persistence is a free, method-specific filter.
METHOD: 1) Frozen CLIP features at layers 6, 12, 18, 24 (the levels where MVFA inserts adapters). 2) Per level, NN distance of each patch to the dataset's normal bank; level threshold = 99th percentile on normal source-validation images. 3) Persistence count c_p = number of levels above threshold. 4) Pseudo-mask = c_p >= 3 on abnormal images (2 and 4 as ablations). 5) train_zero.py unchanged (Focal + Dice). Cost: four NN searches per image, one-off.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; level-4 only; any level; persistence >= 2, 3, 4. Metrics: pseudo-mask precision, recall, Dice per dataset, trained pixel AUROC, Dice. Falsified if persistence >= 3 does not raise precision by 15 points at less than 10 points recall loss.

Idea B:
TITLE: Rank-based detection-to-segmentation distillation inside MVFA
SUMMARY: Keep the idea of teaching the segmentation branch with the detection branch's patch evidence, but replace KL distillation of sharpened distributions with a pairwise ranking loss that only asks the segmentation map to order patches as the detection map does.
HYPOTHESIS: Rank-based distillation recovers at least as much of the mask-supervised pixel AUROC as KL distillation and is less sensitive to the teacher's scale: varying the sharpening temperature from 0.05 to 0.5 changes pixel AUROC by less than 1 point for rank distillation versus more than 2 points for KL distillation.
RATIONALE: The parent's framing is kept: image labels reach the segmentation branch through the detection branch. The technique changes from matching sharpened probability distributions, which depends on the detection map's scale and a sharpening temperature, to matching patch orderings, which is what pixel AUROC measures and what the detection map is reliable for. Pairwise ranking losses (as in learning-to-rank and in AUC optimisation) are scale-free, so the segmentation branch learns where lesions are without inheriting the detection branch's calibration.
METHOD: 1) Detection branch trained as in MVFA; 5-epoch warm-up. 2) On each abnormal image, sample 256 patch pairs (p, q) with D(p) - D(q) > delta (delta = 0.1 x the image's D range). 3) Loss = mean softplus(-(S(p) - S(q)) / tau) with tau = 0.1; for normal images, BCE of all patches toward 0. 4) Weight 1 relative to the det loss. 5) Ablation: KL distillation (parent) with temperatures 0.05, 0.1, 0.5. Hyper-parameters as MVFA.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); pixel metrics on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; checkpoints and thresholds selected on source validation only; mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std. Conditions: true masks; KL distillation at three temperatures; rank distillation. Metrics: pixel AUROC, Dice, image AUROC, sensitivity of pixel AUROC to temperature. Falsified if rank distillation is worse than the best KL setting by more than 1 point.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: The winner filters pseudo-masks by persistence across exactly the four CLIP levels MVFA adapts, a free, training-free and method-specific test of whether a patch is a lesion or a rare normal pattern, whereas the other is a small variation of distillation whose benefit is limited to temperature robustness.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
